newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Vzla Congress legally okays Cerro Negro oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Vzla Congress legally okays Cerro Negro oil deal.

text.p: Venezuela's joint session of Congress on Thursday approved the legal framework for the $2.6 billion Cerro Negro oil venture between state oil subsidiary Lagoven, Mobil and Veba in the Orinoco belt, congressional sources said.
The vote, the last step before final approval, followed the earlier, similar approval of the $3.5 billion Hamaca venture involving state subsidiary Corpoven with ARCO, Phillips and Texaco.

Final approval of both deals will bring to four the number of approved Orinoco projects aimed at exploiting an estimated 270 billion barrels of heavy and extra-heavy recoverable reserves in the region.
Virgilio Avila Vivas, president of the Senate Committee of Energy and Mines, said the projects would probably be approved finally within the next two weeks.

Two more projects are on the drawing board, bringing the total number to six with a projected cumulative investment of $17 billion. They are innovative both from a technical and financial perspective and constitute a major plank in Venezuela's opening of its oil industry to private capital.
